WISHLY PRACTICAL GUIDE · DIGITAL INVITATIONS

How to Create a Digital Birthday Invitation Website

Plan a digital birthday invitation page with clear event details, a welcoming message, a suitable design and a link guests can open on mobile.

A digital birthday invitation website gives guests one place to read the essential details and understand the mood of the celebration. It can be more expressive than a plain text message, but it still needs to be clear: guests should quickly find the date, time, venue and the best way to ask questions.

✦Wishly GuidePractical product guides · About this publication
Digital Invitations8–10 min readPublished 17 November 2026

Decide what guests need to know first

Start with the details that affect whether someone can attend. Confirm the event date, start time, time zone if guests are in different places, venue name, full address and any practical instructions. If the location is difficult to find, add a recognisable landmark or a map link in the message you send with the invitation.

Make the event type clear: children’s birthday, milestone celebration, family gathering or casual party. The wording and design should set expectations about the tone, dress code and whether children or additional guests are welcome. Do not leave important conditions hidden in decorative text.

  • Honouree’s name and celebration type.
  • Date, start time and venue/address.
  • Dress code, parking, age guidance or other relevant notes.

Write a warm invitation with a clear call to action

Use a friendly opening that welcomes guests and explains why the celebration matters. Then present the essential event details in a scannable format. Finish with a clear next step: for example, ask guests to reply to the host through the contact method you provide if they have a question or need to confirm attendance.

Do not describe a response form or RSVP system as part of Wishly unless the chosen invitation template explicitly provides it. If you need an RSVP count, use a separate form, messaging thread or event tool and put the relevant instructions on the invitation page.

  • Keep the invitation headline short.
  • Make date, time and location easy to find.
  • State how guests should contact the host or confirm attendance.

Choose a visual style that matches the party

A child’s birthday may call for bright colours and playful illustrations, while a milestone dinner may suit a more restrained design. Use the honouree’s favourite colours or a theme they enjoy, but keep enough contrast for text to remain readable. The invitation should look celebratory without making the practical details hard to find.

If you add photographs, use images that are appropriate for all invited guests. Do not include private family pictures or a home address in an image unless the page is being shared only with trusted recipients. Check the design on mobile because invitations are often opened from chat apps.

  • Match colours to the party theme.
  • Keep event details in live readable text where possible.
  • Check the page on a phone before sharing.

Create the invitation with Wishly

Open Wishly and select Invitation Cards or another suitable occasion/template that matches your event. Choose a design and edit the fields available in that template. Depending on the selected layout, you may be able to personalise wording, images and other supported media; not every template contains the same controls.

Use Preview to verify that the date, time and address are correct and readable. Save your work and publish the invitation when you are ready. Open the live URL yourself and review it as a guest would, rather than relying only on the editor screen.

  • Select Invitation Cards or the closest suitable template.
  • Add event details to the supported fields.
  • Preview carefully, save and publish the invitation page.

Share the invitation and manage replies

Send the link in the same channel your guests use—such as a family group, direct message or email. Include a brief note so people know who is invited and whether the link is intended for them personally. For a large guest list, keep a separate list of replies so the host can plan seating, food and other arrangements.

A public invitation link can be forwarded. If guest privacy matters, share it only with the intended people and consider password protection where available. Do not publish guest phone numbers, children’s personal details or other sensitive information on the page.

  • Use a channel appropriate for the guest list.
  • Track replies separately if the template has no RSVP tool.
  • Keep private event details limited to invited guests.

Use a final event checklist before sending

A simple review prevents most invitation mistakes. Read every detail once for accuracy and again from a guest’s perspective: is the location understandable, is the start time clear, and does the invitation explain what to do next? Ask one other person to proofread it if the celebration is important or the guest list is large.

If any event detail changes after sending, update the live page where possible and send a correction message to guests. Do not assume that every guest will revisit the link automatically. Directly notify people about important changes to time or location.

  • Verify date, time, time zone and address.
  • Check spelling of names and contact details.
  • Send a direct update if any important detail changes.

Frequently asked questions

What should a digital birthday invitation include?

Include the honouree, event date, start time, venue and address, relevant instructions and a clear way to contact the host or confirm attendance.

Can Wishly collect RSVPs?

Do not assume every Wishly invitation template includes RSVP collection. Check the chosen template; if it does not provide the feature, use a separate form or messaging channel.

Can I share the invitation through WhatsApp?

You can share the published link through messaging apps such as WhatsApp. Add a short note explaining the invitation.

Can I update an invitation after sharing it?

You can edit your project and republish/update it through the available workflow. Send guests a direct message if a key detail changes.

Final thoughts

A good digital invitation balances personality with practical information. Make the details easy to find, test the page on a phone and communicate any updates directly so guests can plan with confidence.
